children: climbed 0.9% in Wednesday's trading despite receiving a downgrade to Hold from Buy with a $2.90 price target at Jefferies, as crude oil prices jumped.

shares have tripled YTD, which Jefferies analyst Mark Wilson said now captures much of the material improvement in the company's balance sheet that high oil prices, solid operations and disposals, and an equity raise have delivered in 2026.
ending 2026 with just under $2.3B in net debt and below 2x geared, assuming $100/bbl Brent into year-end, after starting the year with nearly $3B net debt and 5.5x geared.
The analyst said the material improvement in Kosmos'

balance sheet has been helped by the oil price tailwind, solid operations at GTA and much-improved Jubilee performance, the Equatorial Guinea disposal for $127M cash on completion, the equity raise for $185M gross proceeds at $1.90/share, and the $350M Nordic Bond with an 11.25% coupon and 2031 maturity issued in January.
While total net asset value reduces when combining all variables, it is also significantly derisked, Wilson said, adding that further upside could come with a new growth leg such as GTA Phase 2.

title: Kosmos Energy cut to Hold at Jefferies after stock soars 200% YTD
